title: ci: split lint/test/release workflows, bump Node.js to 20, improve cache hygiene
author: Jordan Lee
description: Motivation: CI has grown slow and brittle as more integrations were added to a single monolithic workflow. This PR splits lint/test/release into smaller reusable workflows, upgrades primary CI runners to Node.js 20, and tightens cache keys and retention to reduce flakiness and storage usage. Changes: 1) Split the large .github/workflows/ci.yml into three reusable workflows: workflows/lint.yml, workflows/test.yml, workflows/release.yml. 2) Introduced reusable workflow templates under .github/workflows/reusable/ to share matrix and checkout steps across SDK packages. 3) Bumped all Node.js job runners from 18 to 20 and upgraded pinned actions (actions/checkout, actions/setup-node) to latest major versions. 4) Improved caching hygiene: normalized cache keys, fallback heuristics, and reduced restore/save windows for npm/yarn and pip caches. 5) Switched heavy integration tests to a dedicated runner label and added concurrency controls to avoid burst queueing. 6) Added explicit retry logic for flaky network steps and a small suite of faster smoke checks for PR validation. Checklist: - [x] Split workflows and add reusable templates - [x] Upgrade Node.js images and actions - [x] Validate caches across redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript, redwood, redwood-examples - [x] Run full CI and fix failures - [x] Update docs snippet referencing CI badges Notes: Kept changes minimal in package repos; most changes are in workflows. This is intended as a hygiene and speedup change rather than functional change. Related: ENG-4321 (CI performance), SUP-7881 (customer flake report).
commits: split workflows: lint/test/release and add reusable templates
ci: bump Node 18 -> 20 in workflows and update actions pins
ci(cache): normalize cache keys and add fallback logic
ci: route integration tests to dedicated runner label with concurrency

release_notes: Refactor CI into smaller reusable workflows, bump Node 18 -> 20 for CI runners, improve cache keys and reduce flakiness. No product changes.
